page: Amazon Web Services m6g.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by 64-bit arm64 AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the ARM Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. As a dedicated bare-metal instance without a hypervisor layer, it provides direct physical access to all 64 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with single-threaded execution (1 thread per core). The hardware configuration includes 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, yielding a standard balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per core, along with a 25Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong parallel throughput and caching efficiency. The server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng (97,214.24), Clang software compilation (44,453.0), Redis SET operations reaching 74.25 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput of 48.58 GB/sec. Cached memory read throughput is exceptionally high at 3,792.04 GB/sec across L1, L2, and L3 caches. However, single-core execution shows lower relative performance, scoring 986.0 in Geekbench single-core and showing weak results in single-threaded compression and decompression routines. Large language model text generation also tests in the lower percentile ranks.

By dispensing with hypervisor virtualization overhead while maintaining an arm64 power-efficient footprint, m6g.metal offers strong multi-threaded resource density. It is well matched for horizontally scaled backend workloads, container fleets, Clang-based CI/CD build farms, high-throughput in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and high-concurrency web serving environments that leverage high core counts rather than peak single-thread execution speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server featuring 64 physical arm64 cores based on the AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. It offers 256 GB of DDR4 RAM, establishing a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, and operates with a 25 Gbps network interface without local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-threaded performance, achieving high marks in software compilation with Clang, Redis throughput exceeding 74 million operations per second, and 48.58 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-threaded processing and LLM text generation fall into lower benchmark tiers. The lack of hypervisor overhead makes m6g.metal an efficient platform for multi-threaded microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and high-concurrency web applications.
